terms.definition: A message from a sanitizer that names two unsynchronized accesses to the same memory.

import Dispatch; import Synchronization
let c = Mutex(0)
DispatchQueue.concurrentPerform(
    iterations: 50) { _ in
    c.withLock { $0 += 1 } }  // fixed
print(c.withLock { $0 })

video.description:
Learn to explain how to talk about finding data races and slow async work with Xcode tools: Data Race Report, Thread Sanitizer & Concurrency Instrument, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Data Race Report - A message from a sanitizer that names two unsynchronized accesses to the same memory.
Thread Sanitizer - An Xcode diagnostic that watches memory while the app runs and reports data races.
Concurrency Instrument - An Instruments template that shows tasks and actors and their waits on a timeline.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Data Race Report, Thread Sanitizer & Concurrency Instrument in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Data Race Report, Thread Sanitizer, Concurrency Instrument 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Data Race Report - A message from a sanitizer that names two unsynchronized accesses to the same memory.
한국어: Data Race Report: 같은 메모리에 대한 동기화되지 않은 두 접근을 알려 주는 새니타이저의 메시지

Thread Sanitizer - An Xcode diagnostic that watches memory while the app runs and reports data races.
한국어: Thread Sanitizer: 앱이 실행되는 동안 메모리를 감시해 데이터 레이스를 알려 주는 Xcode 진단 도구

Concurrency Instrument - An Instruments template that shows tasks and actors and their waits on a timeline.
한국어: Concurrency Instrument: 태스크와 액터, 그리고 대기 시간을 타임라인으로 보여 주는 Instruments 템플릿

dialogue.title: A crash that happens sometimes

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the app crashes sometimes, and I cannot find the reason.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It sounds like a data race. Turn on Thread Sanitizer in the scheme.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It watches memory while the app runs and reports data races.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It stopped and showed a long data race report. I do not understand it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Read the data race report from the top. It names two accesses to the same memory.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One access is in `Tally`. The other is outside the actor.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then move that access inside the actor, or call it with `await`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fixed. Now the screen is slow sometimes, too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use the concurrency instrument. It shows tasks and actors and their waits on a timeline.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I can see which task waits for the actor?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Thread Sanitizer finds races, and the concurrency instrument finds waits.
